findings.title: Unilateral credit line reduction with good cause
findings.triggered_by: By giving you written notice, we may reduce your Credit Line from time to time, or, with good cause, revoke your card and terminate this Agreement.
findings.description: Unilateral credit line reduction with good cause
findings.search_query_used: credit card change in terms unilateral modification account cancellation
findings.plain_language_explanation: The credit card company can lower your credit limit or cancel your card anytime with just written notice. They don't need your permission.
findings.user_impact: Your available credit could suddenly drop, potentially maxing out your card if you carry a balance.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: If you carry a $3,000 balance on a $5,000 limit and they reduce it to $3,200, you're suddenly near your max limit, hurting your credit score and limiting spending power.

recommended_actions.action: Pay down existing balances to create buffer room before limit reductions
Apply for backup credit card with different issuer as emergency option
Set up balance alerts to monitor credit utilization if limits change
recommended_actions.contact: Your credit card company or credit monitoring service

findings.title: Discretionary payment allocation by credit union
findings.triggered_by: Subject to applicable law, your payments may be applied to what you owe the Credit Union in any manner the Credit Union chooses.
findings.description: Credit union has unilateral discretion over payment allocation which could disadvantage consumer
findings.search_query_used: subject applicable your payments applied what credit union credit card consumer rights
findings.plain_language_explanation: The credit union can decide how to apply your payments across different debts you owe them, rather than letting you choose where your money goes.
findings.user_impact: Since you carry balances, they could apply payments to lower-rate debts first, keeping high-rate debts longer.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: You make a payment intending it for your high-interest credit card, but they apply it to your low-interest loan instead, costing you more in interest over time.

recommended_actions.action: Ask for written payment allocation policy and request specific payment directing options
Consider paying each debt separately with designated payments to ensure proper allocation

findings.triggered_by: Balances you transfer from other creditors will be treated as cash advances for the purpose of this agreement and will be subject to your standard cash advance APR unless a promotional APR applies.

findings.plain_language_explanation: Balance transfers are being charged like cash advances, which have higher interest rates and fees than regular purchases or typical balance transfers.

recommended_actions.action: Shop for cards with true balance transfer offers before signing

findings.triggered_by: If you transfer your balances you may lose your grace period on purchases.

findings.plain_language_explanation: When you move debt from another card to this one, you lose the time to pay new purchases without interest charges.
findings.user_impact: Since you carry balances, new purchases will immediately start earning interest charges.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: You transfer $5,000 debt then buy $500 groceries. That $500 starts earning 25% interest right away instead of having 25 days to pay it off first.
